question: For IPv4 subnets whose network has an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list each subnet’s name and CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IPv4 group (ordered by standard attribute ID), and the range and variance of the DNS nameserver order values configured for that subnet. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH IPv4SubnetDNSOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SharedNetworkSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), SharedIPv4SubnetDNSAndRBACDetails AS ( SELECT sns.subnet_name, sns.subnet_cidr, sns.rbac_target_tenant, sns.window_column, ids.order_range, ids.order_variance FROM SharedNetworkSubnets sns JOIN IPv4SubnetDNSOrderStats ids ON ids.subnet_name = sns.subnet_name JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NAME = sns.subnet_name WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT * FROM SharedIPv4SubnetDNSAndRBACDetails ORDER BY subnet_name, rbac_target_tenant;
sub_questions: For each subnet name, compute the range and variance of the DNS nameserver order values configured for that subnet, considering only IPv4 subnets.

For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the subnet name, its CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, and the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID.
sub_sqls: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC;

SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared';

question: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list only those whose total connections are greater than the average total connections across all “haproxy” load balancers, and return the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, total connections, and the same row number ordered by load balancer name using a window frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' ), ProviderAverages AS ( SELECT pra.PROVIDER_NAME, AVG(stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS) AS avg_total_connections FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID GROUP BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ) SELECT i.loadbalancer_name, i.vip_address, i.bytes_in, i.total_connections, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb2 ON lb2.NAME = i.loadbalancer_name AND lb2.VIP_ADDRESS = i.vip_address JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra2 ON lb2.ID = pra2.RESOURCE_ID WHERE i.total_connections > ( SELECT avg_total_connections FROM ProviderAverages WHERE ProviderAverages.PROVIDER_NAME = pra2.PROVIDER_NAME ) ORDER BY i.loadbalancer_name;
sub_questions: For load balancers provided by “haproxy”, list the load balancer name, VIP address, bytes in, and total connections, and assign row numbers ordered by load balancer name using a window frame of 2 preceding and 1 following rows.
sub_sqls: SELECT lb.NAME AS loadbalancer_name, lb.VIP_ADDRESS AS vip_address, stats.BYTES_IN AS bytes_in, stats.TOTAL_CONNECTIONS AS total_connections, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY lb.NAME ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS stats JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON stats.LOADBALANCER_ID = lb.ID JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy';

question: For each port status, list the status, the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, and the total number of distinct security groups involved. Do not repeat the status if it is the same as the previous row. Include a final TOTAL row across all statuses, considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(status) OVER (ORDER BY status_sort, status) = status THEN NULL ELSE status END AS status, coefficient_of_variation, distinct_security_groups FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.status END AS status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.status END AS status, AVG(i.coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation, COUNT(DISTINCT sgpb.security_group_id) AS distinct_security_groups FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY status_sort, status;
sub_questions: For each port status, show the status and the coefficient of variation of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have a security group port binding and a port security binding.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For the top 10 tenants with the most distinct DOWN ports on network ID `0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d`, return the tenant ID, total distinct ports, whether they have any security-group-bound ports, the count of DOWN ports on that network, and the number of qualifying DOWN ports for tenant `98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57` (ports whose standard attribute ID is above that tenant’s average), but only include tenants where more than 75% of their total ports are DOWN on that network. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH TenantPortSummary AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')) SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.security_group_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_security_groups FROM ports p LEFT JOIN inner_cte ON p.network_id = inner_cte.network_id AND p.mac_address = inner_cte.mac_address GROUP BY p.tenant_id ORDER BY total_ports DESC LIMIT 10 ), TenantDownPortWindowed AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), TenantAvg AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS avg_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p2 ON p2.ID = i.port_id JOIN TenantAvg ta ON ta.tenant_id = i.tenant_id WHERE p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > ta.avg_standard_attr_id ), TenantDownPortCounts AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS down_ports_in_network FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.network_id IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d') GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT tps.tenant_id, tps.total_ports, tps.has_security_groups, tdc.down_ports_in_network, COUNT(DISTINCT tdpw.port_id) AS qualifying_down_ports_for_tenant_98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57 FROM TenantPortSummary tps JOIN TenantDownPortCounts tdc ON tps.tenant_id = tdc.tenant_id LEFT JOIN TenantDownPortWindowed tdpw ON tps.tenant_id = tdpw.tenant_id WHERE (tdc.down_ports_in_network * 1.0 / NULLIF(tps.total_ports, 0)) > 0.75 GROUP BY tps.tenant_id, tps.total_ports, tps.has_security_groups, tdc.down_ports_in_network ORDER BY tps.total_ports DESC;

question: For networks that have more ports in status 'DOWN' with port security enabled than the average across all networks, list the network ID and the total number of such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 ), NetworkDownSecurePorts AS ( SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM PORTS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED = 1 GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID ) SELECT network_id, total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled FROM NetworkDownSecurePorts WHERE total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled > ( SELECT AVG(total_down_ports_with_port_security_enabled) FROM NetworkDownSecurePorts );

question: For the top 10 device owners (status = 'DOWN') with the most distinct security-group-bound ports in tenant '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', show the port status, device owner, distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, whether any ports have multiple security group bindings, and—using the same non-shared-network ports filtering based on standard attributes—also include the earliest standard attribute updated timestamp and the deviation of that (status, device owner) port count from the overall average across all such groups. sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), avg_cte AS (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, (i.port_count - a.avg_port_count) AS deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT spb2.security_group_id) > COUNT(DISTINCT p2.id) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_multi_sg_bindings FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p2 ON p2.status = i.port_status AND p2.device_owner = i.device_owner AND p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') JOIN securitygroupportbindings spb2 ON p2.id = spb2.port_id GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT q2.port_status, q2.device_owner, q2.port_count AS distinct_port_count, q2.min_standard_attr_id, q2.has_multi_sg_bindings, q1.earliest_standard_attr_update, q1.deviation_from_avg_port_count FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.port_status = q2.port_status AND q1.device_owner = q2.device_owner ORDER BY q2.port_count DESC;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, which port IDs (with their tenant ID, host, VIF type, port name, MAC address, allocated IP address, and subnet ID) appear when combining (1) the row number over IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row and (2) the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address? sql: WITH down_ports_bindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), down_ports_ipavg AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT dpb.port_id, dpb.tenant_id, dpb.host, dpb.vif_type, dpb.ip_address, dpb.window_column AS row_number_by_ip_window, dpi.port_name, dpi.mac_address, dpi.subnet_id, dpi.window_column AS avg_port_id_by_ip_window FROM down_ports_bindings dpb JOIN down_ports_ipavg dpi ON dpb.port_id = dpi.port_id AND dpb.ip_address = dpi.ip_address;

sub_sqls: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN';

SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS;

question: For the IPv4 subnet whose ID is `012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48`, return the subnet name along with (1) the dense rank of its associated standard attribute when ordered by the standard attribute UPDATED_AT timestamp using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows, and (2) the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of routes per subnet. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH SubnetWindowRanks AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') ), SubnetRouteStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ) SELECT swr.NAME AS subnet_name, swr.window_column, srs.route_count_range, srs.route_count_variance, srs.route_count_stddev FROM SubnetWindowRanks AS swr JOIN SubnetRouteStats AS srs ON srs.subnet_name = swr.NAME ORDER BY swr.NAME, swr.window_column;

question: For tenant ID `17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7`, among ports on host `drive-59` whose running sum of `STANDARD_ATTR_ID` within each `VIF_TYPE` group (ordered by `STANDARD_ATTR_ID`) is greater than the overall average running sum for those ports, show each port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, VIF type, running sum and its overall average, plus the port’s port-security binding count, total enabled port-security flags, the average binding-count benchmark across the tenant’s administratively up ports, and the binding category (HIGH/LOW/AVERAGE). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each port as 'HIGH_BINDINGS' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_BINDINGS' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_BINDINGS'.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7')) SELECT i.PORT_ID, i.TENANT_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, b.VIF_TYPE, i.window_column, (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON i.PORT_ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE i.window_column > (SELECT AVG(window_column) FROM inner_cte) ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), AverageBindings AS ( SELECT AVG(binding_count) AS avg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT ic.port_id, ic.tenant_id, ic.mac_address, ic.binding_count, ic.port_security_enabled_total, ab.avg_binding_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN ic.binding_count > ab.avg_binding_count * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_BINDINGS' WHEN ic.binding_count < ab.avg_binding_count * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_BINDINGS' ELSE 'AVERAGE_BINDINGS' END AS binding_category FROM inner_cte ic CROSS JOIN AverageBindings ab ) SELECT q1.port_id, q1.tenant_id, q1.mac_address, q1.vif_type, q1.window_column AS running_standard_attr_id_sum, q1.avg_window_column AS avg_running_sum_over_filtered_ports, q2.binding_count, q2.port_security_enabled_total, q2.benchmark AS avg_binding_count_benchmark, q2.binding_category FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.port_id = q2.port_id ORDER BY q1.vif_type, q1.window_column DESC, q2.binding_count DESC;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, group the results by port status and port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) and list the port status, a label of the port-security setting ('Enabled' if true, 'Disabled' otherwise), and the number of ports. Include subtotals per port status and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), PortSecurityRollup AS ( SELECT p.status, CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN 'Enabled' ELSE 'Disabled' END AS port_security_status, COUNT(DISTINCT inner_cte.port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte JOIN ports AS p ON inner_cte.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status, port_security_status ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(port_security_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE port_security_status END AS port_security_status, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports FROM PortSecurityRollup GROUP BY status, port_security_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each network status, show the status and compute the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the network MTU values, considering only networks that have an associated security binding and an RBAC entry with action = 'access_as_shared', and excluding shared networks (i.e., exclude networks whose ID appears in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, AVG(n.MTU) AS avg_mtu, STDDEV(n.MTU) AS mtu_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON nsb.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS rbac ON n.ID = rbac.OBJECT_ID WHERE n.MTU IS NOT NULL AND rbac.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' AND n.ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY mtu_stddev DESC;

sql: WITH SubnetPoolsAndMaxStdAttrNext2 AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') ), SubnetStdAttrDenseRankWindow AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') ) SELECT sp.NAME AS subnet_name, sp.TENANT_ID, sp.NETWORK_ID, sp.IP_VERSION, sp.CIDR, sp.GATEWAY_IP, sp.ENABLE_DHCP, sp.FIRST_IP, sp.LAST_IP, sp.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sr.window_column AS dense_rank_by_updated_at_window FROM SubnetPoolsAndMaxStdAttrNext2 sp JOIN SubnetStdAttrDenseRankWindow sr ON sp.NAME = sr.NAME;

question: For each IPv4 subnet that has a positive average DNS nameserver order, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first and last IP, the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows (ordered by subnet ID), the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of DNS nameserver order values for that subnet, and keep only those subnets whose coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such IPv4 subnets; order the results by the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetPoolWindowStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), SubnetDnsOrderVariation AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT spws.NAME AS subnet_name, spws.TENANT_ID, spws.NETWORK_ID, spws.IP_VERSION, spws.CIDR, spws.GATEWAY_IP, spws.ENABLE_DHCP, spws.FIRST_IP, spws.LAST_IP, spws.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sdov.coefficient_of_variation FROM SubnetPoolWindowStats spws JOIN SubnetDnsOrderVariation sdov ON spws.NAME = sdov.subnet_name ORDER BY sdov.coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.ip_version, i.cidr, i.gateway_ip, i.enable_dhcp, i.first_ip, i.last_ip, i.max_standard_attr_id_next2, i.coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i WHERE i.coefficient_of_variation > (SELECT AVG(i2.coefficient_of_variation) FROM inner_cte i2) ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC;

WITH SubnetPoolWindowStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), SubnetDnsOrderVariation AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT spws.NAME AS subnet_name, spws.TENANT_ID, spws.NETWORK_ID, spws.IP_VERSION, spws.CIDR, spws.GATEWAY_IP, spws.ENABLE_DHCP, spws.FIRST_IP, spws.LAST_IP, spws.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sdov.coefficient_of_variation FROM SubnetPoolWindowStats spws JOIN SubnetDnsOrderVariation sdov ON spws.NAME = sdov.subnet_name ORDER BY sdov.coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, show the down port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, and the average admin_state_up over a window of 2 preceding and 2 following rows (partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), along with the matching administratively up port’s name, MAC address, port security enabled flag, and its row number over a window of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row (ordered by MAC address), matching the two sets by MAC address; additionally, for each matched pair, include the deviation of the down port’s windowed average admin_state_up from the overall average of that windowed average across all down ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), AdminUpPortsWithSecurity AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT dp.NAME AS down_port_name, dp.MAC_ADDRESS AS down_mac_address, dp.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS down_admin_state_up, dp.HOST AS binding_host, dp.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, dp.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f, au.port_name AS admin_up_port_name, au.mac_address AS admin_up_mac_address, au.port_security_enabled, au.window_column AS row_number_window_2p_1f FROM DownPortsWithBindings dp JOIN AdminUpPortsWithSecurity au ON dp.MAC_ADDRESS = au.mac_address ORDER BY dp.MAC_ADDRESS), overall_avg AS (SELECT AVG(avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f) AS overall_avg_admin_state_up_window FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.down_port_name, i.down_mac_address, i.down_admin_state_up, i.binding_host, i.vif_type, i.avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f, i.admin_up_port_name, i.admin_up_mac_address, i.port_security_enabled, i.row_number_window_2p_1f, (i.avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f - oa.overall_avg_admin_state_up_window) AS deviation_from_overall_avg_windowed_admin_state_up FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa ORDER BY i.down_mac_address;

For ports that are administratively up, list the port name, MAC address, and port security status, and assign row numbers ordered by MAC address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row.

SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1;

WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), AdminUpPortsWithSecurity AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT dp.NAME AS down_port_name, dp.MAC_ADDRESS AS down_mac_address, dp.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS down_admin_state_up, dp.HOST AS binding_host, dp.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, dp.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_window_2p_2f, au.port_name AS admin_up_port_name, au.mac_address AS admin_up_mac_address, au.port_security_enabled, au.window_column AS row_number_window_2p_1f FROM DownPortsWithBindings dp JOIN AdminUpPortsWithSecurity au ON dp.MAC_ADDRESS = au.mac_address ORDER BY dp.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For ACTIVE networks, show the network name, status, and admin_state_up along with the RBAC action and target tenant, but only return those networks whose number of RBAC entries is greater than the average RBAC-entry count across all ACTIVE networks. Also include a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), NetworkRbacCounts AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, COUNT(r.id) AS total_rbacs FROM networks n JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN NetworkRbacCounts c ON c.network_id = n.id WHERE c.total_rbacs > (SELECT AVG(total_rbacs) FROM NetworkRbacCounts);
sub_questions: Show each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up together with the RBAC action and target tenant for that network, plus a dense rank within each network (partitioned by network ID and ordered by network ID). Only include networks that are ACTIVE.
sub_sqls: SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'

question: For the top 10 (port status, device owner) combinations with the most ports (counting only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and excluding shared networks), show the port status, device owner, total port count, earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, whether any ports in that top-10 combination have floating IPs, and—joined by the same port status—the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of port security binding counts per port (for ports with at least one binding in tenant '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') plus whether tenant ports in that status have any floating IPs. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.port_status AND p.device_owner = i.device_owner JOIN standardattributes sa ON sa.id = p.standard_attr_id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON p.id = f.fixed_port_id WHERE sa.resource_type = 'ports' AND p.network_id NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id WHERE p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT i.status, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ports AS p ON p.status = i.status LEFT JOIN floatingips AS f ON p.id = f.fixed_port_id WHERE p.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY i.status, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev ORDER BY i.binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT q1.port_status, q1.device_owner, q1.port_count, q1.earliest_standard_attr_update, q1.has_floating_ips AS top10_combo_has_floating_ips, q2.binding_count_range, q2.binding_count_variance, q2.binding_count_stddev, q2.has_floating_ips AS tenant_ports_in_status_have_floating_ips FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q2.status = q1.port_status ORDER BY q1.port_count DESC;

sub_questions: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and excluding shared networks (i.e., networks whose IDs appear in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'), return the number of ports and the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp.

For each port status, report the status and the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of port security bindings per port, considering only ports that have at least one port security binding and belong to tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7'.

Among the top 10 (port status, device owner) combinations with the highest number of ports—considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and excluding shared networks (networks whose IDs appear in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b')—return the port status, device owner, total number of ports, the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp, and whether any of those ports have a floating IP allocated.

For each port status, report the status and the range, variance, and standard deviation of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding and belong to tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7'), and also indicate whether ports in that status have any floating IPs allocated.
sub_sqls: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id WHERE p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.port_status AND p.device_owner = i.device_owner JOIN standardattributes sa ON sa.id = p.standard_attr_id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON p.id = f.fixed_port_id WHERE sa.resource_type = 'ports' AND p.network_id NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.earliest_standard_attr_update ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id WHERE p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT i.status, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN ports AS p ON p.status = i.status LEFT JOIN floatingips AS f ON p.id = f.fixed_port_id WHERE p.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY i.status, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev ORDER BY i.binding_count_range DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are also bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port status, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID). Additionally, for each tenant appearing in these results, include the total number of ports they own and the average number of ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT s1.port_id, s1.tenant_id, s1.mac_address, s2.port_status, s2.ip_address, s1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, s2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network FROM Subq1 s1 JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s1.port_id = s2.port_id ORDER BY s1.port_id) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, COUNT(p_all.id) AS total_ports_for_tenant, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_across_all_tenants FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p_all ON p_all.tenant_id = i.tenant_id JOIN (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(id) AS port_count FROM ports GROUP BY tenant_id) AS sub) AS avg_ports GROUP BY i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, avg_ports.avg_port_count ORDER BY i.port_id;

question: For IPv4 subnets, using the detailed subnet-and-route listing as a base, summarize how many result rows fall under each DHCP enabled flag and route presence category (label as 'Has Routes' when a subnet has at least one associated route row, otherwise 'No Routes'). Include subtotals per DHCP flag and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetDetails AS (SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP AS allocation_first_ip, sd.LAST_IP AS allocation_last_ip, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, srd.DESTINATION AS route_destination, srd.NEXTHOP AS route_nexthop, srd.window_column AS route_dense_rank_within_subnet FROM SubnetDetails sd LEFT JOIN SubnetRouteDetails srd ON sd.NAME = srd.subnet_name AND sd.CIDR = srd.subnet_cidr AND sd.FIRST_IP = srd.FIRST_IP AND sd.LAST_IP = srd.LAST_IP ORDER BY sd.NAME, srd.window_column, srd.DESTINATION), RoutePresenceSummary AS (SELECT ic.ENABLE_DHCP, CASE WHEN ic.route_destination IS NOT NULL THEN 'Has Routes' ELSE 'No Routes' END AS route_presence, COUNT(*) AS total_rows FROM inner_cte ic GROUP BY ic.ENABLE_DHCP, route_presence) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(ENABLE_DHCP) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(ENABLE_DHCP AS CHAR) END AS enable_dhcp, CASE WHEN GROUPING(route_presence) = 1 AND GROUPING(ENABLE_DHCP) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE route_presence END AS route_presence, SUM(total_rows) AS total_rows FROM RoutePresenceSummary GROUP BY ENABLE_DHCP, route_presence WITH ROLLUP;

Show each subnet route’s destination and next hop together with the subnet name and CIDR, plus the allocation pool’s first and last IP. Also include a dense rank within each subnet (partitioned by subnet ID) ordered by the subnet ID. Only include IPv4 subnets.

For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet’s name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, and allocation pool first/last IP, along with the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current subnet row and the next two rows (ordered by subnet ID). Also show any associated subnet routes (destination and next hop) and the dense-rank value within each subnet for those routes.

question: Across all DOWN ports that share a MAC address with an administratively-up port, return the DOWN port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, its running sum of standard attribute ID within its security group, plus the administratively-up port’s name, port security enabled flag, and MAC-address-ordered row number; also include the deviation of each DOWN port’s running-sum value from the overall average running-sum across all such matched DOWN ports, and only keep rows where the running-sum value is greater than 0. sql: WITH sg_admin_up_ports AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(security_group_binding_count) AS avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.port_name, i.security_group_binding_count, i.dns_record_count, (i.security_group_binding_count - a.avg_sg_binding_count) AS deviation_from_avg_sg_binding_count FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a), sg_down_ports_above_avg AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), sg_counts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, c.down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN sg_counts AS c ON i.security_group_id = c.security_group_id WHERE c.down_ports > (SELECT AVG(down_ports) FROM sg_counts)) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.port_id) AS admin_up_ports_with_sg_bindings_count, COUNT(DISTINCT d.port_id) AS down_ports_in_security_groups_above_avg_count FROM sg_admin_up_ports a CROSS JOIN sg_down_ports_above_avg d;

WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports_for_tenant_in_sg, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_per_tenant_in_sg FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON inner_cte.port_id = p.ID JOIN ( SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT COUNT(p2.ID) AS port_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb2 JOIN PORTS p2 ON sgpb2.PORT_ID = p2.ID WHERE sgpb2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' GROUP BY p2.TENANT_ID ) AS sub ) AS avg_ports ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY inner_cte.port_id, inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.ip_address, inner_cte.window_column, p.TENANT_ID, avg_ports.avg_port_count;

question: For the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports, list each tenant’s ID and DOWN port count, along with their ACTIVE networks (network ID, network name, admin_state_up, MTU, standard attribute updated_at, and the row number per tenant ordered by network name) and the tenant’s DOWN ports (port ID, MAC address, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type ordered by standard attribute ID). sql: WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ), top_tenants AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM subq1 GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY down_port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT tt.tenant_id, tt.down_port_count, s2.network_id, s2.network_name, s2.admin_state_up, s2.mtu, s2.standard_attr_updated_at, s2.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, s1.port_id, s1.mac_address, s1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type FROM top_tenants tt JOIN subq2 s2 ON s2.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id LEFT JOIN subq1 s1 ON s1.tenant_id = tt.tenant_id ORDER BY tt.down_port_count DESC, tt.tenant_id, s2.window_column, s2.network_name, s1.port_id;

question: For ACTIVE (non-shared) networks, list each network’s name, status, and admin_state_up along with its RBAC action, target tenant, and dense-rank-by-network-ID window column, and also include the overall average, range (max minus min), and variance of subnet IP version for RBAC entries with the action set to 'access_as_shared' (considering only IP versions 4 and 6). Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH rbac_ip_version_stats AS ( SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) AND n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC ), active_network_rbac_details AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND n.id NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) ) SELECT d.name, d.status, d.admin_state_up, d.action, d.target_tenant, d.window_column, s.rbac_action, s.avg_ip_version, s.ip_version_range, s.ip_version_variance FROM active_network_rbac_details d CROSS JOIN rbac_ip_version_stats s WHERE s.rbac_action = 'access_as_shared';

a.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_mtu_cte a ), ports_subq AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), VifTypeCounts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS ports_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), OverallWindowAvg AS ( SELECT AVG(window_column) AS overall_avg_window_column FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.PORT_ID, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.VNIC_TYPE, i.TENANT_ID, i.NETWORK_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.STATUS, i.DEVICE_OWNER, i.window_column, vtc.ports_in_vif_type, (i.window_column - owa.overall_avg_window_column) AS deviation_from_overall_window_avg FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN VifTypeCounts AS vtc ON i.VIF_TYPE = vtc.VIF_TYPE CROSS JOIN OverallWindowAvg AS owa ) SELECT n.network_id, n.network_name, n.tenant_id, n.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up, n.mtu, n.standard_attr_updated_at, n.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, n.deviation_from_avg_mtu, p.PORT_ID, p.HOST, p.VIF_TYPE, p.VNIC_TYPE, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER, p.window_column AS port_windowed_avg_standard_attr_id, p.ports_in_vif_type, p.deviation_from_overall_window_avg FROM networks_subq n JOIN ports_subq p ON p.NETWORK_ID = n.network_id AND p.TENANT_ID = n.tenant_id;

sql: WITH shared_subnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), ipv4_dense_ranks AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.rbac_target_tenant, ss.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids_ipv_group, idr.window_column AS dense_rank_by_updated_at_ipv4 FROM shared_subnets ss JOIN ipv4_dense_ranks idr ON idr.NAME = ss.subnet_name;

sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance, STDDEV(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_stddev FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC ), overall_avgs AS ( SELECT AVG(avg_ip_version) AS overall_avg_ip_version, AVG(ip_version_variance) AS overall_avg_variance, AVG(ip_version_stddev) AS overall_avg_stddev FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.ACTION, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_variance, i.ip_version_stddev, (i.avg_ip_version - sql: WITH NetworkStatusSecurityBindingStats AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC ), DefaultExternalNetworksByTenant AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, e.IS_DEFAULT, n.TENANT_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, n.MTU, n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, MIN(n.MTU) OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.TENANT_ID) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 AND n.ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) ) SELECT den.NETWORK_ID, den.IS_DEFAULT, den.TENANT_ID, den.NAME, den.STATUS, den.ADMIN_STATE_UP, den.MTU, den.STANDARD_ATTR_ID, den.window_column AS min_mtu_within_tenant, nssbs.port_security_enabled_variance, nssbs.port_security_enabled_stddev FROM DefaultExternalNetworksByTenant den JOIN NetworkStatusSecurityBindingStats nssbs ON den.STATUS = nssbs.network_status;

DESTINATION) AS destination_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY subnet_name, subnet_cidr, NEXTHOP) t GROUP BY subnet_name, subnet_cidr ), top_routes_and_pools AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, AS subnet_cidr, COUNT(DISTINCT r.DESTINATION) AS total_routes, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_allocation_pools FROM SUBNETS s LEFT JOIN SUBNETROUTES r ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID LEFT JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON p.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN inner_cte i ON i.subnet_name = s.NAME AND i.subnet_cidr = s.CIDR WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48') GROUP BY s.ID, s.NAME, s.CIDR ORDER BY total_routes DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT t.subnet_id, t.subnet_name, t.subnet_cidr, t.total_routes, max_dest_per_nexthop m ON m.subnet_name = t.subnet_name AND m.subnet_cidr = t.subnet_cidr ORDER BY max_nexthop_destination_share DESC, t.total_routes DESC;

question: From the top 10 RBAC actions restricted to the access_as_shared permission (ranked by the range of referenced subnets’ IP version), show each action’s name, average subnet IP version, IP-version range (max minus min), variance of subnet IP version, and whether any referenced subnet has DHCP enabled—only including actions whose average IP version is greater than 4. sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) AND n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC) SELECT rbac_action, avg_ip_version, ip_version_range, ip_version_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE avg_ip_version > 4 ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) AND n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC ) SELECT i.rbac_action, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.ip_version_variance, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 THEN s.ID END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_dhcp_enabled_subnets FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n ON n.ACTION = i.rbac_action JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = n.OBJECT_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) AND n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY i.rbac_action, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.ip_version_variance ORDER BY i.ip_version_range DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT q2.rbac_action, q2.avg_ip_version, q2.ip_version_range, q2.ip_version_variance, q2.has_dhcp_enabled_subnets FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.rbac_action = q2.rbac_action ORDER BY q2.ip_version_range DESC;

question: For each ACTIVE network that has an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC target tenant, dense-rank within the network ID, the network MTU and its deviation from the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks, and also include (by matching on status) the status-level average and variance of MTU computed from external networks shared via 'access_as_shared'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.status, AVG(n.mtu) AS avg_mtu, VARIANCE(n.mtu) AS mtu_variance FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.network_id = n.id JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE r.action = 'access_as_shared' AND n.mtu IS NOT NULL GROUP BY n.status ORDER BY mtu_variance DESC) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, AVG(avg_mtu) AS avg_mtu, AVG(mtu_variance) AS mtu_variance FROM inner_cte GROUP BY status WITH ROLLUP ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveNetworkMTU AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.mtu FROM networks n WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ), AverageActiveMTU AS ( SELECT AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM ActiveNetworkMTU ) SELECT i.name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.action, i.target_tenant, i.window_column, anm.mtu, (anm.mtu - aam.avg_mtu) AS deviation_from_avg_mtu FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.name AND n.status = i.status AND n.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up JOIN ActiveNetworkMTU anm ON anm.network_id = n.id CROSS JOIN AverageActiveMTU aam ) SELECT q2.name, q2.status, q2.admin_state_up, q2.action, q2.target_tenant, q2.window_column, q2.mtu, q2.deviation_from_avg_mtu, q1.avg_mtu AS status_level_avg_mtu_for_external_shared, q1.mtu_variance AS status_level_mtu_variance_for_external_shared FROM q2 JOIN q1 ON q1.status = q2.status WHERE q2.action = 'access_as_shared' ORDER BY q2.deviation_from_avg_mtu DESC;

question: For each VIF type, show the VIF type, the number of DOWN ports, the average of the per-port windowed average admin_state_up (2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), and the average (across the involved hosts) variance of port standard attribute IDs for DOWN ports that have an IP allocation. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up, AVG(hsav.standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsav ON dpw.HOST = hsav.HOST GROUP BY dpw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_ports_count DESC;

question: For each tenant that has ports in DOWN status, list the tenant ID, the number of DOWN ports, the average number of DOWN ports across all such tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
sql: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), TenantDownPorts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(p.id) AS total_down_ports FROM PORTS AS p JOIN inner_cte AS ic ON ic.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageDownPorts AS (SELECT AVG(total_down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPorts) SELECT tdp.tenant_id, tdp.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tdp.total_down_ports > adp.avg_down_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tdp.total_down_ports < adp.avg_down_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantDownPorts AS tdp CROSS JOIN AverageDownPorts AS adp;

question: For subnets that have DHCP enabled and whose subnet ID is in ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48'), what is the minimum subnet IP version and the total number of IP allocation pools associated with those subnets, considering only subnets that also have at least one subnet route? sql: SELECT MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS min_ip_version, SUM(CASE WHEN p.ID IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_allocation_pools FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.ENABLE_DHCP = 1 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48');

question: For networks that are marked as default external networks (IS_DEFAULT = 0) and have the RBAC permission action set to 'access_as_external', list the (non-repeated) network name, its dense rank (ordered by the RBAC action using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows), the RBAC tenant ID and target tenant, the total number of matching networks, the average number of matching networks per tenant, and the ratio of total matching networks to the average per tenant (rounded to 2 decimals).
sql: WITH sq1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_external' ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(inner_cte.NAME) OVER (ORDER BY inner_cte.NAME, r.TENANT_ID) = inner_cte.NAME THEN NULL ELSE inner_cte.NAME END AS name, inner_cte.window_column, r.TENANT_ID AS rbac_tenant_id, r.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN NETWORKS n ON n.NAME = inner_cte.NAME JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON r.OBJECT_ID = n.ID AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_external' ORDER BY inner_cte.NAME, r.TENANT_ID ), sq2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY r.ACTION ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_external' ), tenant_counts AS ( SELECT n.TENANT_ID, COUNT(*) AS tenant_network_count FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_external' GROUP BY n.TENANT_ID ), avg_counts AS ( SELECT AVG(tenant_network_count) AS avg_networks_per_tenant FROM tenant_counts ) SELECT inner_cte.NAME, inner_cte.window_column, totals.total_matching_networks, avg_counts.avg_networks_per_tenant FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_matching_networks FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.ID = r.OBJECT_ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 AND r.ACTION = 'access_as_external' ) AS totals ON 1 = 1 JOIN avg_counts ON 1 = 1 ) SELECT sq1.name, sq1.window_column, sq1.rbac_tenant_id, sq1.rbac_target_tenant, sq2.total_matching_networks, sq2.avg_networks_per_tenant, ROUND(sq2.total_matching_networks / NULLIF(sq2.avg_networks_per_tenant, 0), 2) AS total_to_avg_ratio FROM sq1 JOIN sq2 ON sq2.NAME = sq1.name AND sq2.window_column = sq1.window_column ORDER BY sq1.name, sq1.rbac_tenant_id;

sql: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(vif_type) OVER (ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, mac_address) = vif_type THEN NULL ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, name, mac_address, admin_state_up, host, window_column, down_ports_count, avg_window_column FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.vif_type END AS vif_type_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.vif_type) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.vif_type END AS vif_type, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.window_column, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(i.window_column) AS avg_window_column FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.vif_type, i.name, i.mac_address, i.admin_state_up, i.host, i.window_column WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY vif_type_sort, vif_type, mac_address;

sql: WITH q1 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57')), VifTypeCounts AS ( SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE ), AverageVifTypePorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM VifTypeCounts ) SELECT i.PORT_ID, i.HOST, i.VIF_TYPE, i.VNIC_TYPE, i.TENANT_ID, i.NETWORK_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.STATUS, i.DEVICE_OWNER, i.window_column, vtc.total_ports, avp.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN vtc.total_ports > avp.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN vtc.total_ports < avp.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM inner_cte i JOIN VifTypeCounts vtc ON i.VIF_TYPE = vtc.VIF_TYPE CROSS JOIN AverageVifTypePorts avp ), q2 AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL AND ia.IP_ADDRESS IN ('10.150.64.113/8') GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ), StatusPortCounts AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS distinct_ports FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL AND ia.IP_ADDRESS IN ('10.150.64.113/8') GROUP BY p.STATUS ), AverageVariance AS ( SELECT AVG(standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_variance FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.STATUS, i.standard_attr_id_variance, spc.distinct_ports, (i.standard_attr_id_variance - av.avg_variance) AS deviation_from_avg_variance FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN StatusPortCounts AS spc ON i.STATUS = spc.status CROSS JOIN AverageVariance AS av ORDER BY i.standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT q1.PORT_ID, q1.HOST, q1.VIF_TYPE, q1.VNIC_TYPE, q1.TENANT_ID, q1.NETWORK_ID, q1.MAC_ADDRESS, q1.STATUS, q1.DEVICE_OWNER, q1.window_column, q1.total_ports, q1.benchmark, q1.user_category, q2.standard_attr_id_variance, q2.distinct_ports, q2.deviation_from_avg_variance FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.STATUS = q2.STATUS;

question: For IPv4 subnets whose DNS nameserver order range is greater than the average order range across all IPv4 subnets, return each subnet name along with its DNS nameserver order range, order variance, coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the order values, and the deviation of that coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets. sql: WITH RangeVarianceSubnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC) SELECT subnet_name, order_range, order_variance FROM inner_cte WHERE order_range > (SELECT AVG(order_range) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY order_range DESC ), CoeffVarDeviationSubnets AS ( WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(coefficient_of_variation) AS avg_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.coefficient_of_variation, (i.coefficient_of_variation - a.avg_coefficient_of_variation) AS deviation_from_avg FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg DESC ) SELECT rvs.subnet_name, rvs.order_range, rvs.order_variance, cvd.coefficient_of_variation, cvd.deviation_from_avg FROM RangeVarianceSubnets rvs JOIN CoeffVarDeviationSubnets cvd ON rvs.subnet_name = cvd.subnet_name ORDER BY rvs.order_range DESC, cvd.deviation_from_avg DESC;

sql: WITH down_ports_sg AS (WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), sg_counts AS ( SELECT security_group_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.security_group_id, i.window_column, c.down_ports FROM inner_cte AS i JOIN sg_counts AS c ON i.security_group_id = c.security_group_id WHERE c.down_ports > (SELECT AVG(down_ports) FROM sg_counts)), host_drive59_tenants AS (WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT i.PORT_ID) AS total_ports, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT psb.PORT_ID) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte AS i LEFT JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON i.PORT_ID = psb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.TENANT_ID ORDER BY total_ports DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.mac_address, d.security_group_id, d.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, d.down_ports AS down_ports_in_security_group, h.total_ports AS total_ports_on_drive_59_for_tenant, h.has_port_security_enabled FROM down_ports_sg AS d JOIN host_drive59_tenants AS h ON d.tenant_id = h.tenant_id;

sql: WITH DnsOrderStats AS (SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC), RoutePoolDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT rpd.subnet_name, rpd.subnet_cidr, rpd.DESTINATION, rpd.NEXTHOP, rpd.FIRST_IP, rpd.LAST_IP, rpd.window_column, dos.avg_dns_order, dos.dns_order_variance FROM RoutePoolDetails rpd JOIN DnsOrderStats dos ON rpd.subnet_name = dos.subnet_name ORDER BY dos.dns_order_variance DESC, rpd.subnet_name, rpd.window_column;

question: For ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and whose network is not shared (exclude networks listed in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'), for each (port status, device owner) group return the port count, the earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, the overall average port count across all returned groups, and each group’s deviation from that average. sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') ), AdminUpPortBindingAndDnsCounts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND p.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ) SELECT dpsg.security_group_id, COUNT(DISTINCT dpsg.port_id) AS down_port_count, MAX(au.security_group_binding_count) AS max_security_group_binding_count_among_admin_up_ports, SUM(au.dns_record_count) AS total_dns_record_count_for_admin_up_ports, ROUND( SUM(au.dns_record_count) / NULLIF(MAX(au.security_group_binding_count), 0), 2 ) AS dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN AdminUpPortBindingAndDnsCounts au ON au.port_id = dpsg.port_id AND au.tenant_id = dpsg.tenant_id WHERE dpsg.tenant_id IN ('98333a1a28e746fa8c629c83a818ad57') GROUP BY dpsg.security_group_id ORDER BY dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio DESC) , NetworkSecurityGroupRatios AS ( SELECT p.network_id, i.security_group_id, i.dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio FROM inner_cte i JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.security_group_id = i.security_group_id JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = sgpb.port_id ) SELECT network_id, MAX(dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio) AS max_dns_records_per_max_binding_ratio FROM NetworkSecurityGroupRatios GROUP BY network_id;

sql: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), PortStatusSecurityBindingStats AS (SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.binding_count_range, s.binding_count_variance, s.binding_count_stddev FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortStatusSecurityBindingStats s ON s.status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY d.ip_address) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports_with_ip_and_psb, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips, MAX(i.binding_count_range) AS down_binding_count_range, MAX(i.binding_count_variance) AS down_binding_count_variance, MAX(i.binding_count_stddev) AS down_binding_count_stddev FROM inner_cte i JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = i.port_id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.fixed_port_id = i.port_id GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports_with_ip_and_psb DESC LIMIT 10;
